question: Between the years of 1950 and 1990, in which year did U.S personal saving rates (measured as household saving as a percent of after-tax income) peak?
raw_response:
I can now see the Personal Saving chart clearly. The line peaks at its highest point — reaching nearly 9.5 percent — between the 1970 and 1975 gridlines. The peak is just before the 1975 tick mark, which corresponds to approximately 1973-1974. Looking carefully, the maximum point sits roughly two ticks before 1975, placing it at 1973.

The line rises through the early 1970s, hits its absolute highest point (~9.4-9.5%) right around 1973, then drops sharply afterward. This matches the well-known historical fact that the U.S. personal saving rate peaked around 1973-74.

Examining the tick spacing: gridlines at 1970 and 1975 with the peak sitting clearly closer to 1975 but distinctly before it — the apex is at 1973.

<FINAL_ANSWER>1973</FINAL_ANSWER>
